followup_reviews.Research finding: The NBR strike is supported as one included campaign with two separately evidenced facility phases, without expanding it to every Bangladesh border. P1 covers Sonamasjid–Mahadipur goods imports/exports; P2 covers Benapole–Petrapole goods imports/exports. Passenger restrictions are not established. Both directions have facility-specific evidence. Both P1 and P2 retain complete shutdown from Saturday 28 June to Monday 30 June 2025 and two-calendar-day differences. Named port sources and actual truck counts support Monday return. Earlier partial pen-down hours and Sunday-night withdrawal are not substituted for observed full-stop dates. The overlapping phases are not added into four days. Policy and socioeconomic demands / Jobs, services and livelihoods remains supported by staff reform, promotion, neutrality and dignity demands attributed to the NBR movement. Both current source bodies were freshly read: BSS quotes the Sonamasjid operator; Jago News quotes Benapole’s director and supplies dated inbound/outbound truck counts. These are separate facility observations, not evidence for every other port. Both phases remain individually unlocated, with no national geometry and no invented shared coordinate for the two different crossings.
